Design a detailed, concrete implementation plan for a new feature in the KasirKu POS app (Next.js App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind + Supabase, at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu). Do not write code — produce a step-by-step plan with exact file paths, schema, and function signatures. I already did extensive exploration; use the facts below as ground truth rather than re-deriving them, but you may Read specific files listed below to verify exact current code before finalizing signatures.

## Feature being added
A THIRD business type, `'tiket'` (alongside existing `'fnb'` and `'retail'`), for venue/attraction ticketing (kolam renang, playground, tempat wisata). This is a distinct "kasir" model — not products, but numbered admission tickets — confirmed by the user via clarifying questions:

- Two ticket categories exist per business, configurable (not hardcoded), e.g. "Pengunjung" (visitor) and "Penunggu" (companion) — each has its OWN continuous serial-number sequence (never resets).
- Ticket price depends on day type: weekday vs "hari libur" (holiday) — holiday = Saturday/Sunday automatically, OR a manually-marked date (owner can flag specific calendar dates, e.g. national holidays, via a settings UI).
- There's a paid membership system: `members` are subscription/card-based customers (name, phone, a member code, validity period `valid_from`/`valid_until`). Members get a special ticket price per category (or free access) instead of the weekday/holiday price. A member's ticket still gets a serial number (for attendance/reconciliation tracking) — it's not a free pass with zero record.
- Ticket prices ARE subject to the business's existing tax_rate/service_rate settings (same fields already on `businesses`: tax_enabled, tax_rate, service_enabled, service_rate), same formula as the existing product checkout.
- User wants two reports: (1) total active member count, (2) sales report filterable/groupable by ticket category + serial-number range + date range, for reconciling physical ticket usage against system sales.

## Ground truth from my exploration (verified by reading the actual files)

**business_type column**: `supabase/migrations/20260702100100_businesses_and_cashiers.sql` line 7: `business_type text not null check (business_type in ('fnb', 'retail')),` — inline unnamed check constraint, so Postgres auto-names it `businesses_business_type_check`. This migration is ALREADY APPLIED to the live Supabase DB (per project convention: migrations are pasted manually into the Supabase dashboard SQL editor, no linked CLI) — so it must NOT be edited in place; a NEW migration file must ALTER the existing constraint (`drop constraint if exists businesses_business_type_check` then re-add with the third value).

**Existing generic infra that's reusable as-is for the ticket business type** (do NOT rebuild these):
- `cashiers` table + PIN auth + roles (kasir/manajer) — business-type agnostic.
- `shifts` table (open/close, opening_cash, cash_sales, etc.) — business-type agnostic, just a business_id/cashier_id relation, no product coupling.
- `attendance`, `payroll` modules — agnostic.
- POS entry flow `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/page.tsx` → `pin-screen.tsx` (PIN entry) → `open-shift-screen.tsx` (opening cash) — both fully generic, no product references, reusable verbatim. Only the final step (`pos-screen.tsx`, the actual cart/checkout UI, 1328 lines, tightly coupled to `products`) is NOT reusable for tickets — a new client component is needed for the ticket-selling screen, but it should be reached via the SAME `/business/[businessId]/pos` route (page.tsx already branches server-side on `business.business_type`; extend that branch to render a new `TicketPosScreen` instead of `PosScreen` when businessType === 'tiket', after the same PinScreen/OpenShiftScreen gates).
- Existing `checkout_transaction` RPC pattern (latest version in `supabase/migrations/20260704200000_customers.sql`, lines 40-254) is the model to mirror for a new `checkout_ticket_transaction` RPC: security definer, validates `private.owns_business()`, validates active cashier, validates active shift exists (reuses the SAME `shifts` table — no new shift concept needed), generates an invoice number via count-based sequence (existing pattern, accepted risk in this codebase), does the work in a loop, inserts a header row + child rows.
- Existing `void_transaction` RPC (`supabase/migrations/20260703100000_void_transaction_rpc.sql`) is the model for a new `void_ticket_transaction` RPC — same manager-PIN-verification-via-crypt pattern (`c.pin_hash = extensions.crypt(p_manager_pin, c.pin_hash)`), same `for update` row lock before flipping voided/voided_at/void_reason/voided_by. For tickets there's no stock to restore, just flip the flag (ticket serials stay permanently allocated even if voided, matching physical reality — a printed ticket was already handed out).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/customers/actions.ts` and `add-customer-form.tsx`/`edit-customer-form.tsx` are the CRUD pattern to mirror for the new `members` CRUD pages (server actions with useActionState, soft delete via `deleted_at`, `revalidatePath`, `logActivity` calls — see `src/lib/activity-log.ts` usage).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/reports/period.ts` has `parsePeriod`/`getPeriodRange`/`PERIOD_LABELS` — a WIB-timezone-aware date-range helper already used by reports pages; reuse it for the new ticket sales report's date filter instead of writing new date logic.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/tax-service-form.tsx` + `settings/actions.ts` is the pattern to mirror for a new ticket-category price management form (owner sets price_weekday/price_holiday/member_price per category) and for a holiday-date-marking UI.

**Where `business_type`/`isFnb` currently branches UI** (each needs a new branch or at least must not break for the new type):
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` line ~16-28: fetches `business_type`, computes `isFnb = business.business_type === "fnb"`, passes to `DashboardShell`.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx`: `buildNavGroups(businessId, isFnb)` (lines 11-54) builds the sidebar nav array; `isFnb` also toggles a subtitle string ("Restoran / Kafe / F&B" vs "Retail / Toko") around line 90. This need to become aware of a third type to: hide "Kelola Produk"/"Pelanggan" nav items and show new "Tiket", "Kategori & Harga Tiket", "Anggota" items instead, for `businessType === 'tiket'`.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/page.tsx` (full content already read — lines 1-164): fetches products/open_bills/customers/self_orders unconditionally, computes `isFnb`. For `'tiket'` businesses this whole product-fetching branch should be skipped and ticket_categories/members fetched instead, then render a new `TicketPosScreen`.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/tables/page.tsx` line ~43: hard `notFound()` unless `business_type === "fnb"` — leave as-is, tiket businesses also can't access this page (correct, no change needed beyond confirming it still 404s for 'tiket' too, which it already will since it's an explicit `!== "fnb"` check... wait it needs to also exclude retail already, verify the exact condition still works for a 3-way enum).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` line ~28, ~41, ~115: `isFnb` toggles whether kitchen-printer settings show. Needs a new conditional section for ticket-category price management + holiday calendar when `businessType === 'tiket'`.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/page.tsx` line ~90: `isFnb` affects COGS/reconciliation math — this page queries the `transactions` table for cost-of-goods calculations, which don't apply to ticket sales (no COGS concept for admission tickets). Decide: for 'tiket' businesses, either show a simplified finance page or note this is out of scope for V1 (recommend explicitly treating general Dashboard/Laporan/Laba-Rugi/Keuangan pages as staying scoped to product-based `transactions` only, and building ticket revenue reporting as its own separate, additive report page — do NOT try to unify `transactions` and the new ticket tables inside every existing report page, that's too much scope creep for this task).
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/page.tsx` (main dashboard KPI cards) line ~60: queries `.from("transactions")` unconditionally for today's sales summary — for 'tiket' businesses this always shows zero. Needs a branch: if businessType === 'tiket', query ticket_transactions summary instead for the KPI cards.
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` (list of all businesses) lines ~92, ~143: badge text and a conditional nav link per business_type — needs a third badge/branch.
- `src/app/onboarding/onboarding-form.tsx` (full content read, lines 1-91): radio button picker between fnb/retail — needs a third radio option for "tiket" (venue/wisata). Server-side validation lives in `src/app/onboarding/actions.ts` (`if (businessType !== "fnb" && businessType !== "retail")`) — needs updating too.

**Database types**: `src/lib/types/database.ts` is currently a placeholder (`export type Database = Record<string, never>;`), not actually used for real type inference anywhere critical — do not block the plan on regenerating it, just note that it's out of sync already (pre-existing condition, unrelated to this feature) and the new tables won't appear there either until the user manually runs `supabase gen types` against their live project (per project convention, migrations are pasted manually into the Supabase dashboard, no linked CLI in this sandbox).

## Your task
Produce a concrete implementation plan covering:
1. Exact new migration file (new timestamp after `20260706100000_payroll.sql`, e.g. `20260706200000_ticket_venue.sql`) with full schema: the constraint alter, and CREATE TABLE statements for `ticket_categories`, `members`, `ticket_holidays`, `ticket_transactions`, `ticket_serials` (one row per physical ticket — no separate line-items table needed since price+category can be snapshotted directly on each serial row), RLS policies (mirror the `private.owns_business(business_id)` pattern used everywhere else), and the two RPCs (`checkout_ticket_transaction`, `void_ticket_transaction`) with full plpgsql bodies.
2. Exact list of new page/component files to create for: ticket-selling POS screen, ticket category price settings, holiday calendar settings, members CRUD (list/add/edit/delete), ticket sales history + member-count report.
3. Exact list of existing files to modify and what changes, per the branch points listed above.
4. A suggested nav structure change for `dashboard-shell.tsx` when businessType === 'tiket'.
5. Order of implementation (schema first, then reused-infra wiring, then new UI, then reports) and how to verify each step (what to check in Supabase dashboard after pasting the migration, what to click through in the browser preview).

Keep the plan concrete and scannable — exact file paths, not vague descriptions. Do not include code for every single file (that will be written during implementation), but DO include the full SQL for the migration since that's the highest-risk, hardest-to-fix-after-the-fact part.

1	-- Module 1: businesses, cashiers — foundation for auth & access.
2	
3	create table public.businesses (
4	  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
5	  owner_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
6	  name text not null,
7	  business_type text not null check (business_type in ('fnb', 'retail')),
8	  address text,
9	  phone text,
10	  npwp text,
11	  logo_url text,
12	  tax_enabled boolean not null default false,
13	  tax_rate numeric(5, 2) not null default 0,
14	  service_enabled boolean not null default false,
15	  service_rate numeric(5, 2) not null default 0,
16	  auto_lock_enabled boolean not null default true,
17	  auto_lock_minutes int not null default 5,
18	  recovery_code_hash text,
19	  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
20	);
21	
22	create index businesses_owner_id_idx on public.businesses (owner_id);
23	
24	alter table public.businesses enable row level security;
25	
26	create policy "Owner has full access to own businesses"
27	on public.businesses for all
28	using (owner_id = auth.uid())
29	with check (owner_id = auth.uid());
30	
31	-- Reusable RLS predicate: does the current user own the business that a row belongs to?
32	-- security definer + stable + fixed search_path so it can be inlined efficiently by the
33	-- planner and safely referenced from every table's RLS policy instead of repeating the
34	-- `business_id in (select id from businesses where owner_id = auth.uid())` subquery.
35	-- Defined here (not in the extensions migration) because it needs `businesses` to exist.
36	create or replace function private.owns_business(check_business_id uuid)
37	returns boolean
38	language sql
39	security definer
40	stable
41	set search_path = ''
42	as $$
43	  select exists (
44	    select 1 from public.businesses b
45	    where b.id = check_business_id
46	      and b.owner_id = auth.uid()
47	  );
48	$$;
49	
50	-- Cashiers -------------------------------------------------------------
51	
52	create table public.cashiers (
53	  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
54	  business_id uuid not null references public.businesses (id) on delete cascade,
55	  name text not null,
56	  role text not null check (role in ('kasir', 'manajer')),
57	  pin_hash text not null,
58	  active boolean not null default true,
59	  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
60	);
61	
62	create index cashiers_business_id_idx on public.cashiers (business_id);
63	
64	alter table public.cashiers enable row level security;
65	
66	create policy "Owner manages cashiers of own businesses"
67	on public.cashiers for all
68	using (private.owns_business(business_id))
69	with check (private.owns_business(business_id));
70

1	-- Module 12: void transaksi sebagai satu RPC atomik. Hanya manajer (via PIN,
2	-- diverifikasi terhadap pin_hash di database) yang boleh membatalkan.
3	-- Stok produk dikembalikan dari transaction_items, dan stok bahan baku
4	-- dikembalikan dari snapshot transaction_ingredient_consumption — persis
5	-- kebalikan dari checkout_transaction.
6	
7	create or replace function public.void_transaction(
8	  p_business_id uuid,
9	  p_transaction_id uuid,
10	  p_manager_pin text,
11	  p_reason text default null
12	)
13	returns table (voided_by_name text)
14	language plpgsql
15	security definer
16	set search_path = ''
17	as $$
18	declare
19	  v_manager record;
20	  v_tx record;
21	begin
22	  if not private.owns_business(p_business_id) then
23	    raise exception 'not authorized';
24	  end if;
25	
26	  -- Hanya PIN milik manajer aktif dari bisnis ini yang diterima. Pesan error
27	  -- sengaja tidak membedakan "PIN salah" vs "bukan manajer".
28	  select c.id, c.name
29	  into v_manager
30	  from public.cashiers c
31	  where c.business_id = p_business_id
32	    and c.role = 'manajer'
33	    and c.active
34	    and c.pin_hash = extensions.crypt(p_manager_pin, c.pin_hash)
35	  limit 1;
36	
37	  if not found then
38	    raise exception 'PIN salah atau tidak memiliki otorisasi';
39	  end if;
40	
41	  select t.id, t.voided
42	  into v_tx
43	  from public.transactions t
44	  where t.id = p_transaction_id
45	    and t.business_id = p_business_id
46	  for update;
47	
48	  if not found then
49	    raise exception 'transaction not found';
50	  end if;
51	
52	  if v_tx.voided then
53	    raise exception 'transaksi sudah dibatalkan';
54	  end if;
55	
56	  -- Kembalikan stok produk yang terjual (produk yang sudah dihapus dilewati,
57	  -- sama seperti aplikasi lama).
58	  update public.products p
59	  set stock = p.stock + ti.qty
60	  from public.transaction_items ti
61	  where ti.transaction_id = p_transaction_id
62	    and ti.product_id = p.id
63	    and p.deleted_at is null;
64	
65	  -- Kembalikan stok bahan baku yang terkonsumsi resep saat checkout.
66	  update public.ingredients i
67	  set stock = i.stock + tic.qty
68	  from public.transaction_ingredient_consumption tic
69	  where tic.transaction_id = p_transaction_id
70	    and tic.ingredient_id = i.id;
71	
72	  update public.transactions
73	  set voided = true,
74	      voided_at = now(),
75	      void_reason = nullif(left(trim(p_reason), 200), ''),
76	      voided_by = v_manager.id
77	  where id = p_transaction_id;
78	
79	  return query select v_manager.name;
80	end;
81	$$;
82	
83	grant execute on function public.void_transaction(uuid, uuid, text, text) to authenticated;

2	-- to (or compared on) the client. A 4-6 digit PIN has a tiny keyspace, so

6	-- database itself refuses to return that column to these roles.

10	-- call this (checked explicitly, since SECURITY DEFINER bypasses RLS).
11	create or replace function public.create_cashier(
12	  p_business_id uuid,
13	  p_name text,
14	  p_role text,
15	  p_pin text
16	)
17	returns uuid
18	language plpgsql
19	security definer
20	set search_path = ''
21	as $$
22	declare
23	  new_id uuid;
24	begin
25	  if not private.owns_business(p_business_id) then
26	    raise exception 'not authorized';
27	  end if;
28	
29	  if p_role not in ('kasir', 'manajer') then
30	    raise exception 'invalid role';
31	  end if;
32	
33	  if p_pin !~ '^[0-9]{4,6}$' then
34	    raise exception 'PIN harus 4-6 digit angka';
35	  end if;
36	
37	  insert into public.cashiers (business_id, name, role, pin_hash)
38	  values (
39	    p_business_id,
40	    p_name,
41	    p_role,
42	    extensions.crypt(p_pin, extensions.gen_salt('bf'))
43	  )
44	  returning id into new_id;
45	
46	  return new_id;
47	end;
48	$$;
